g1-implement.title: g1 resolution fix: resolve a relative --file against existence-verified candidate roots
g1-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md for this gate and dispatch a subagent invoking constellation-implementer. The change is confined to scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py: replace the 'join the relative --file onto the payload cwd and trust it' resolution with an ordered, VALIDATED candidate-root resolution. Rungs, in order: (0) --file already absolute -> keep today's behaviour, path_source='absolute'; (1) an absolute --worktree <dir> present in the observed command (the engine's claim CLI already accepts it) -> path_source='worktree_opt'; (2) the LAST cd / Set-Location / pushd target parsed out of the observed command text -> path_source='cd_target'; (3) the payload cwd -> path_source='payload_cwd'; (4) every git worktree root registered against project_dir (git worktree list --porcelain) -> path_source='git_worktree'; (5) project_dir -> path_source='project_dir'. A candidate only wins if the resolved file is a VALID CHECKLIST — it must exist AND parse as JSON AND carry the checklist shape — not merely exist, because the old defect has been seeding phantom .agent-work/<work_id>/ directories in the main checkout and a bare exists() can be decoyed by one. No candidate validates -> BIND NOTHING (fail closed). For the RELEASE verb specifically, first try to resolve against the RECORDED binding for this key (unique suffix match) before touching the filesystem, so a release still removes what its claim put there even after the spine is archived or deleted. Record the winning rung as an additive 'path_source' field on the binding entry (additive VALUE field only — the binding KEY shape is untouchable). Normalize MSYS-style '/c/foo' targets to 'C:/foo'. Targeted tests go in tests/test_spine_rail.py and must drive the real payload shapes in tests/fixtures/probe_payloads.jsonl; rung 4 additionally needs a FRESH-SUBPROCESS integration test against a REAL `git worktree add` on disk (a tmpdir repo), never an in-context fixture that hand-injects the root. Wait for and integrate the returned IMPLEMENTER_RESULT as evidence.

g1b-ambiguity.title: g1b: refuse to guess when two trees both hold a valid checklist at the same relative path
g1b-ambiguity.imperative: Fix-now triage of the g1 reviewer's tc1, applied BEFORE the acceptance run so the live fire tests the code that actually ships. The reviewer built the case on disk: when BOTH the main checkout and a worktree hold a valid checklist at the same relative path, rung 3 (payload_cwd) wins over rung 4 (git_worktree) and binds the main checkout's copy -- a CONFIDENT WRONG PATH, which is the exact failure class this issue exists to end. Its reach is real, not theoretical: .agent-work/ is tracked, so committed checklists sit at identical paths in every tree. It is masked today only because rung 2 (cd_target) fires first for a subagent, whose shell cwd resets between bash calls. Make the claim ladder refuse to guess the way resolve_recorded_release_target already does: when more than one candidate root validates and they name DIFFERENT files, bind nothing rather than take the earlier rung -- skip-on-uncertainty, the store's own posture. Rungs 0, 1 and 2 are TOLD-TRUTH (an absolute --file, an absolute --worktree option, an explicit cd target in the command) and must keep winning outright without consulting the later rungs; the ambiguity check governs only the GUESSED rungs, 3 onward. Dispatch an implementer, then have the SAME reviewer that found tc1 confirm the fix and that nothing else regressed.
